minutes.headline: Committee approved Juneteenth holiday, FY23 facility rates, a lunch price rise and a secretarial contract; Turkey Hill left for fall.
minutes.summary: The School Committee voted on Juneteenth contract amendments, a class donation, the employee handbook, facility rental rates, higher school lunch prices and a three-year secretarial contract. It heard the town manager on debt capacity for Turkey Hill and leaned toward a new build without voting, deferring to the fall. A member announced her resignation at the end of the school year.

public_comment.topic: First public comment period: none offered.
Announced resignation from the School Committee effective at the close of the school year to focus on her studies.

budget_items.what_was_said: Seniors donate toward replacing the turf field scoreboard.
Rates updated for the first time since 2019 to cover higher custodial and kitchen salaries; new sites added.
New hourly charge for a monitor if the renting group lacks a safe-food certified person.
Chair recited hourly changes for custodian, kitchen and field monitor.
Student lunch up across the district; adult prices raised as free meal waivers end.
Three-year contract with raises and estimated value.
Town manager outlined debt policy limits and capacity for new debt; Turkey Hill could fit about the stated amount within regular debt.
Roof project carried in capital plan at an old estimate that is likely higher now.

decisions.decision: A letter on free school meals will be drafted from a template and brought to the June 29 meeting.
Presentations will be pre-recorded and posted ahead of meetings on a trial basis.
Insecticide bill discussion deferred until a facilities director is hired.
Turkey Hill direction returns in the fall, with capital planning to include all known costs.
Concession stand operational costs to return at the August 31 meeting.

what_happened.line: The School Committee voted to add Juneteenth as a paid holiday in three staff agreements: custodial, secretary and clerk, and unaffiliated staff.
It approved new facility rental rates, the first update since 2019, and a school lunch price increase, each by roll call.
It ratified a three-year contract with the secretarial union, with the town manager voting along with the committee.
It heard the town manager on debt capacity for Turkey Hill and took no vote; direction on the project returns in the fall.
It voted to draft a letter to state legislators supporting free school meals, to be brought to the June 29 meeting, and a member announced her resignation.

why_it_matters: Facility rental rates and school lunch prices change what groups using school buildings and families buying school lunch pay, and the new secretarial contract adds to the district's labor costs.
The Turkey Hill decision is deferred to the fall, so how the project is financed, and any effect on the town's debt and tax bills, is still undecided.
watch_next: June 29 meeting: the draft letter on free school meals is due back to the committee.
August 31 meeting: concession stand operating costs return; the Turkey Hill direction returns in the fall.
